title: Austin Utility Rates: Phone Company's Defense
summary:
*   City leaders convened a special meeting to hear Southwestern Bell Telephone Company's comprehensive defense against an earlier report critical of its financial practices.
*   The phone company, through its executives and expert witnesses, argued for its accounting methods, property valuations, and revenue calculations, including whether directory advertising profits should factor into local rates.
*   Witnesses, including a CPA and a bank president, presented detailed financial exhibits covering company dividends, external financing, and the overall cost of equity capital.
*   This focused hearing was a key step in the ongoing public discussion and potential policy decisions regarding local telephone service rates in Austin.

The meeting was called to order with Mayor Miller presiding. Roll call: Present:
Councilmen Perry, White, Mayor Miller Absent: Councilmen Bechtol, Palmer (as they were out
of the city) Present also: W. T. Williams, Jr., City Manager; Doren R. Eskew, City
Attorney.
The Mayor announced that this meeting was called to hear the Telephone Company present
statements in answer to DR. ROBERT MONTGOMERY'S report to the
Council on August 5th.
MR. ED CLARK, local Attorney for the Southwestern Bell Telephone Company, thanked the
Council for the privilege of coming back to answer Dr. Robert Montgomery's statements, and
stated the Company had expert witnesses to appear this afternoon.
(Transcript of this hearing made by regular court reporter) MR. ED GOSSETT, General
Counsel, Southwestern Bell Telephone Company, discussed directory advertising as to
whether or not it should be included in the revenues for Austin; the fair value of
property on which a fair rate of return should be allowed; the bookkeeping and accounting
procedures used which have been approved, and which are constantly being examined by the
F.C.C., F.P.C., Rate Making Commissions, etc.; the three types of depreciation referred to
in Dr. Montgomery's report; and the separation procedures used by the Company.
MR. WHITNEY R. HARRIS, General Solicitor, put on the technical testimony with sworn
witnesses, MR. HOWARD T. COX, C.P.A., and President of the Capital National Bank; and MR.
HOUSTON CASKIE, Assistant Treasurer of the Telephone Company. Mr. Harris, in connection
with the testimony, filed the following exhibits:
